title: Runtime upgrade & compatibility orchestration policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: define an operationally actionable semantic versioning and rollout policy for the serving runtime that balances safety and progress. This ticket consolidates rules for what constitutes a breaking change, required deprecation notices, LTS channel guarantees, rollout gates, and the suite of upgrade tooling (CLI, Console assistant, and runtime adapters).
background: We operate a single runtime across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. Historically, small changes to request/response shaping and cache semantics caused expensive client migrations. Teams require a clear, machine-readable contract plus lightweight automation to reduce migration friction while enabling necessary advances (kernel swaps, quantization runtime changes, batching optimizations).
policy_summary: 1) Versioning model: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, where MAJOR increments allow breaking contract changes. MINOR increments may introduce opt-in enhancements and non-breaking additions. PATCH is bugfix-only. 2) LTS channels: we declare an LTS per MAJOR and guarantee API behavioral stability and security fixes for 12 months. 3) Breaking change rules: any change that can cause client code to crash, silently misinterpret payloads, or change semantics of stored/streamed tokens is a breaking change. 4) Deprecation: all deprecations require machine-readable headers and Console notice with at least 90 days for non-critical items, 180 days for customer-facing surface-level changes. 5) Rollout gates: automated canary -> staged ramp -> full rollout with telemetry gates and automated rollback on regressions.
compatibility_classification: We classify changes into three exclusive buckets to guide rollout and migration requirements: 1) Surface-breaking: changes to request/response JSON schema, feature flags that change required parameters. Requires MAJOR bump + migration assistant + migration guide. 2) Behavioral-breaking: changes that alter semantics (KV cache eviction order, default tokenization settings) but do not change wire schema. Requires MINOR or MAJOR (depending on risk), compatibility adapters, and extended canary. 3) Non-breaking: performance improvements, bug fixes, and additive API fields. Can be MINOR or PATCH with standard validation.
deprecation_and_header_spec: All deprecated fields or behavior must be announced via: - HTTP response header: X-Runtime-Deprecation: deprecated-field=exampleField; removal-date=YYYY-MM-DD; migration-url=https://redwood.example.com/migrations/xyz - Telemetry event: runtime.deprecation_announcement with fields (field, removal_date, severity). Console will surface these automatically. Client SDKs must log a warning when the header is observed.
lifecycle_and_lts_guarantees: LTS promises: - No surface-breaking changes for the LTS lifetime (12 months). - Security fixes and critical bugfixes applied with patches. - Migration helpers backported up to 3 months after LTS birth. LTS selection cadence: announced quarterly; customers may opt-in to LTS channel at deployment time.
rollout_gates_and_automation: Standard rollout pipeline: 1) Local integration and unit tests including compatibility sanity suite. 2) Canary (1% traffic) for 24-72 hours with detailed telemetry. 3) Staged ramp: 10% for 24h, 40% for 48h, 100% final. Gates evaluated automatically: error-rate delta, p99 latency delta, token-consistency (random prompt regression checks), embedding-distance drift for embedding models. Gate thresholds configurable per release but default to: error-rate delta <= 0.1%, p99 latency increase <= 5ms, embedding drift <= 2% relative change. Rollouts that fail gates auto-roll back and open an incident ticket with trace links.
tooling_and_migration_assistants: Ship three pieces of tooling: 1) 'compat-check' CLI that checks a client codebase or config against a runtime version (single command returns a categorized list of potential breakages). 2) Console Migration Assistant: guided steps, changelog diff, sample request replays, and one-click temporary adapter toggles for Dedicated customers. 3) Runtime Adapter Library: a thin server-side shim that can translate legacy request formats to the new runtime format for customers on Dedicated/Private. All tools emit standardized telemetry events and suggestions for migration steps.
telemetry_and_signALS: Required telemetry: per-release regression tests (synthetic prompts + golden outputs), production traffic shadowing results, and 'compat-assert' signals from client SDKs on startup. Important signals used by gates: request errors (5xx/4xx), semantic regression count (golden failure against eval set), and gas-cost (token cost delta). Team will maintain a compatibility dashboard with release-level signal history.
developer_experience_and_docs: - Migration docs for every MAJOR with step-by-step migration checklist and example diffs. - Deprecation timeline table for Console and API docs. - SDKs must include a runtime version assertion helper that warns if the server reports an incompatible MAJOR. - Example adapters in GitHub under redwood/runtime-adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Written policy reviewed and approved by Release Engineering and Platform PM
Compatibility classification examples for at least 10 real subsystems (KV, batching, tokenizer, api-schema, embeddings)
compat-check CLI prototype that flags the top 5 surface-breaking patterns
Console Migration Assistant mockups linked and validated in UX review
Automated rollout gates implemented in CI for canary-stage with rollback automation
decision_log: 2026-02-15: Chose MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH model with explicit LTS windows after cross-team review (Release Eng, Infra, PM).
2026-02-24: Agreed to require machine-readable deprecation headers and Console surfacing (Design & Docs sign-off).
2026-03-02: Telemetry gate thresholds drafted; added embedding drift metric for embedding-related releases.
2026-03-10: Prioritized compat-check CLI and Console Migration Assistant for initial milestone.
implementation_plan: Phase 0 (2 wks): Draft spec + doc + stakeholder review
Phase 1 (4 wks): Implement compat-check CLI and standard deprecation header generator
Phase 2 (6 wks): Console Migration Assistant MVP + rollout gate automation in CI
Phase 3 (ongoing): Runtime Adapter library for Dedicated/Private customers and full LTS operationalization
notes: This policy intentionally separates wire-protocol stability (schema) from behavioral guarantees. Some performance-driven changes will require special migration paths (e.g., KV cache rekeying). We expect the first MAJOR bump to accompany the runtime-2.0 performance refactor and will target a coordinated migration window with key customers.
